prompts.web.plan.idea: Suggest 3 different directions for the site. Goal: [site goal]. Audience: [target audience]. Current task: [task]. For each: site type, the visitor's main action, 3–5 key pages, its strengths and risks. Don't invent features that aren't in the description.
prompts.web.plan.spec: Help me turn the idea into a short brief. Goal: [site goal]. Audience: [target audience]. Main action: [main action]. Content already available: [content]. Constraints: [constraints]. Sections: goal and success measure, audience and their tasks, a page list with each page's purpose, first-version features, later features, content and who prepares it, questions to answer before development. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.plan.build: Write up the brief for the site “[site goal]” as a document I can hand to a designer or developer: a page table (name, purpose, blocks, main action), the first-version feature list with done criteria, requirements for [devices] and constraints [constraints]. Don't add paid services or deadlines I didn't mention. Separately mark where my decision is needed. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.plan.review: Review my site plan: [content]. Checklist: is the goal clear, does each page match a task of the audience [target audience], does each page have a main action, are there unnecessary features for the first version, is it all feasible under [constraints]? For each problem suggest a fix and its priority (high, medium, low). Separately list the questions I haven't answered yet.
prompts.web.structure.idea: Suggest 3 site structure options. Goal: [site goal], audience: [target audience]. Task: [task]. For each: a two-level page map, the main menu, pros and cons. If I gave an [example site], analyse only individual qualities (structure, mood, density, navigation) and propose an original solution rather than copying it.
prompts.web.structure.spec: Draw up a detailed sitemap for [site goal]. For each page: a path like /section/page, the menu label (up to 2 words), what's on the page, the main action, where visitors arrive from and where it leads next. Separately: the main menu on desktop and on phone ([devices]) and breadcrumbs for deep pages. Content to place: [content]. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.structure.build: Build the navigation from the agreed sitemap: [content]. Technologies: [technologies]. Needed: main menu, mobile menu, breadcrumbs, footer links. The menu must work with a keyboard, the current item must be marked, and on narrow screens it must not cause horizontal scrolling. If the site already exists, first study the project structure, the technologies in use, any instructions in the repository and the current design. Then give a plan, change only the files that need it and list what you changed. Don't remove existing features or data without my explicit permission. Don't publish the site or change the plan, domain or access without confirmation.
prompts.web.structure.review: Review the site structure: [content]. For the audience [target audience] and the action [main action], answer: can the main action be reached in 3 clicks, are menu labels clear, are there duplicate pages, are there dead ends with no next step, are contacts and key information easy to find? Separate confirmed problems from assumptions. For each, give a fix and a priority.
prompts.web.prototype.idea: Suggest 3 different layouts for the “[page type]” page. Audience: [target audience], main action: [main action]. Task: [task]. For each, describe in words the blocks from top to bottom, what's visible on the first screen and where the eye is led. If I gave an [example site], analyse only individual qualities (structure, mood, density, navigation) and propose an original solution rather than copying it.
prompts.web.prototype.spec: Write a text prototype of the “[page type]” page for [devices]. For each block from top to bottom: purpose, a draft heading, elements (text, image, button, form), what happens on click, the order on a phone. Use only this content: [content]; where something is missing, mark “content needed”. Separately describe the states: loading, error, empty. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.prototype.build: Build an interactive prototype of the “[page type]” page from this description: [content]. Style: [style], colours: [colours]. I need phone and desktop versions, working buttons and transitions between states. Use placeholder text instead of real data and don't add logos or characters I have no rights to. Task: [task]. If the tool offers to publish or use a paid feature, ask me first.
prompts.web.prototype.review: Compare two layouts of the “[page type]” page: option A — [content], option B — [example site]. Criteria: clarity of the main action “[main action]”, hierarchy, density, usability on [devices], accessibility. A table with 1–5 scores and reasons. Finally, what to take from each option, without picking a winner for me.
prompts.web.style.idea: Suggest 3 visual directions for the site “[site goal]” for [target audience]. Desired mood: [style]. Task: [task]. For each: 3 words for the mood, a palette in words with colour roles, a font pairing (serif or sans), the character of images, what to avoid. No random gradients or meaningless decoration. If I gave an [example site], analyse only individual qualities (structure, mood, density, navigation) and propose an original solution rather than copying it.
prompts.web.style.spec: Draft a design system foundation for a site in the “[style]” style with colours [colours]. A token table: colours (background, surface, text, secondary text, accent, success, error) for light and dark themes, fonts and a size scale (headings 1–3, body, caption), spacing (4 or 8 px step), radii, shadows. Rules for buttons (primary, secondary, text), cards, fields and messages, including hover, focus and disabled states. State which colour–background pairs meet 4.5:1 contrast. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.style.build: Implement the design tokens in the project: [content]. Technologies: [technologies]. Move colours, fonts, spacing and radii into variables, add a dark theme via the system setting and a toggle, and replace hard-coded values in components with tokens. Task: [task]. If the site already exists, first study the project structure, the technologies in use, any instructions in the repository and the current design. Then give a plan, change only the files that need it and list what you changed. Don't remove existing features or data without my explicit permission. Don't publish the site or change the plan, domain or access without confirmation.
prompts.web.style.review: Review the site's visual style: [content]. Checklist: text–background contrast (list pairs that fail 4.5:1), whether buttons and fields are consistent across pages, how many fonts and sizes are used, any decoration that hurts reading, whether errors and confirmations look consistent, whether the dark theme works. For each problem, a specific fix and a priority.
prompts.web.ux.idea: Suggest 5 ways to improve the usability of the “[page type]” page. Audience: [target audience], main action: [main action]. Page description: [content]. Task: [task]. For each: what to change, why it helps, how much effort it takes (low, medium, high).
prompts.web.ux.spec: Write out the “[main action]” flow step by step for [target audience]. For each step: what the person sees, what they do, the button text, possible errors and the message for each (what happened and what to do), a hint or input example, the loading state and the success confirmation. Mark steps that could be removed or merged. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.ux.build: Improve the usability of the “[page type]” page in the project: [content]. Technologies: [technologies]. Do: clear button text, hints and examples in fields, error messages next to the field with an explanation, loading, empty-list and “nothing found” states, confirmation of a successful action. Task: [task]. If the site already exists, first study the project structure, the technologies in use, any instructions in the repository and the current design. Then give a plan, change only the files that need it and list what you changed. Don't remove existing features or data without my explicit permission. Don't publish the site or change the plan, domain or access without confirmation.
prompts.web.ux.review: Assess the page as a first-time visitor from [target audience]. Description or code: [content]. Find where they might get lost: an unclear main action, confusing words, extra steps, forms without hints, errors without explanation, no feedback after clicking. Table: problem, where, why it hurts, fix, benefit, priority. Separate what's visible in the description from assumptions.
prompts.web.responsive.idea: Analyse the page description: [content]. Suggest 2 ways to rebuild it for phones ([devices]): block order, how the menu, images and buttons behave. Find elements that could cause horizontal scrolling or become too small. Don't remove important features. Task: [task].
prompts.web.responsive.spec: Write a responsive spec for the “[page type]” page: breakpoints (based on content, not device models); for each width, grid columns, block order, menu style, heading sizes, how tables (scroll inside or cards), images and forms behave, a minimum tap target of 44×44 px. Mark what must not disappear on phones. Content: [content]. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.responsive.build: Make the “[page type]” page responsive. Project: [content]. Technologies: [technologies]. Use a flexible grid, relative font sizes, responsive images, a keyboard-accessible mobile menu, and tables that scroll inside their container. Eliminate horizontal scrolling from 320 px up. Task: [task]. If the site already exists, first study the project structure, the technologies in use, any instructions in the repository and the current design. Then give a plan, change only the files that need it and list what you changed. Don't remove existing features or data without my explicit permission. Don't publish the site or change the plan, domain or access without confirmation.
prompts.web.responsive.review: Write a responsive checklist for the “[page type]” page at 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 px: horizontal scrolling, wrapping of long words and headings, buttons not cut off, the menu opens and closes, tables and images don't overflow, forms are easy to fill in, key content is present, tap target sizes. For each item, how to check and how to fix if it fails. Page description: [content].
prompts.web.a11y.idea: What accessibility problems are most common on “[page type]” pages? My page description: [content]. Task: [task]. List 8 likely problems: for each, who it affects (blind users, low-vision users, people with motor or cognitive difficulties), how to check it and how to fix it.
prompts.web.a11y.spec: Write accessibility requirements for the “[page type]” page to WCAG 2.2 AA: h1–h3 heading structure, landmarks (header, nav, main, footer), labels for all fields and icon buttons, focus order and visible focus, 4.5:1 contrast for text and 3:1 for large text and UI elements, form errors in text and tied to the field, alt text for images, captions for video, screen-reader announcements for page changes. Content: [content]. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.a11y.build: Fix the accessibility of the “[page type]” page in the project: [content]. Technologies: [technologies]. Do: correct heading levels, landmarks, labels and aria-label where needed, visible focus, keyboard operation (including menus and dialogs), errors linked to fields, meaningful alt text, and no meaning conveyed by colour alone. Task: [task]. If the site already exists, first study the project structure, the technologies in use, any instructions in the repository and the current design. Then give a plan, change only the files that need it and list what you changed. Don't remove existing features or data without my explicit permission. Don't publish the site or change the plan, domain or access without confirmation.
prompts.web.a11y.review: Check accessibility from the description or code: [content]. Make a prioritised fix list: first what fully blocks people (unreachable by keyboard, unlabelled field, unreadable text), then what makes things harder, then improvements. For each: what's wrong, who it affects, the WCAG criterion, the fix. Separate what's confirmed from what needs manual checking.
prompts.web.copy.idea: Suggest 3 copy options for the “[page type]” page in different tones: neutral, friendly, formal. Audience: [target audience]. What we offer: [content]. Task: [task]. For each: a heading, a subheading and button text for the action “[main action]”. No unverified promises or stock phrases like “best” and “unique”.
prompts.web.copy.spec: Write copy for every element of the “[page type]” page from these facts: [content]. Audience: [target audience]. Tone: [style]. Needed: block headings, short descriptions, button text (verb + outcome), field labels and hints, a 5-question FAQ, error messages (what happened and what to do), confirmations and empty states. Use only the facts I gave; where they're missing, write “[to confirm]”. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.copy.build: Replace the text on the “[page type]” page in the project with the agreed copy: [content]. Technologies: [technologies]. Keep the markup and styles, update button, hint and message text, and check long text doesn't break the layout on phones. If the site has several languages, don't change translations without my consent; mark where a new translation is needed. Task: [task]. If the site already exists, first study the project structure, the technologies in use, any instructions in the repository and the current design. Then give a plan, change only the files that need it and list what you changed. Don't remove existing features or data without my explicit permission. Don't publish the site or change the plan, domain or access without confirmation.
prompts.web.copy.review: Review the site copy: [content]. Find: exaggerated or unverifiable promises, bureaucratic wording, words too hard for [target audience], vague buttons like “Submit” and “Next” without context, contradictions in timing, prices and terms, error messages without explanation. Table: fragment, problem, fixed version. Don't invent new facts.
prompts.web.graphics.idea: For the “[page type]” page of the site “[site goal]”, suggest where images are needed and of what kind: photo, illustration, icon or diagram. Site style: [style], colours: [colours]. Task: [task]. For each spot: why an image is needed, what it shows, the format and aspect ratio, and how to keep it from interfering with text.
prompts.web.graphics.spec: Write a brief for a set of illustrations in one consistent style for the site: [style], palette: [colours]. For each illustration ([content]): subject, composition, angle, lighting, background, aspect ratios for desktop and phone, where to leave space for text. Rules for the whole set: line weight, level of detail, what repeats across all images. No text inside images and no recognisable characters or logos. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.graphics.build: Create an original illustration for the “[page type]” page. It should help explain “[content]”, suit the audience [target audience] and match the “[style]” style. Palette: [colours]. Format: [constraints]. Task: [task]. Leave empty space for a heading. Avoid text inside the image and recognisable characters or logos unless I have the rights to use them.
prompts.web.graphics.review: Review the images on the page from this description: [content]. Questions: does each image help explain the content or is it decoration, does the background interfere with reading, do the images match in style, is there alt text, are the files too heavy for phones, are there recognisable people without consent or other people's logos? For each problem, a fix.
prompts.web.landing.idea: Suggest three original first-screen options for the landing page “[site goal]”. Audience: [target audience]. The visitor's main task: [main action]. Tone: [style]. Task: [task]. For each, write a heading, subheading and button text, and describe the layout. Don't use unverified promises or stock marketing phrases.
prompts.web.landing.spec: Outline the landing page “[site goal]” for [target audience]. Blocks in order: first screen, the visitor's problem, how it works (3–4 steps), benefits through real tasks, evidence (only from my facts: [content]), FAQ, call to action “[main action]”, footer. For each block: purpose, a draft heading, content, what the visitor does. Where there are no facts, write “[needs confirmation]”. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.landing.build: Build the landing page “[site goal]” from the agreed structure: [content]. Style: [style], colours: [colours], devices: [devices]. Use only my text and facts, with no invented reviews, numbers or logos. The “[main action]” button must be visible on the first screen and at the end of the page. Task: [task]. Show me the result first; don't publish, connect a domain or turn on paid features without my confirmation.
prompts.web.landing.review: Review the landing page from the first screen to the end: [content]. Audience: [target audience], action: [main action]. Answer: is it clear within 5 seconds what this is and who it's for; are there unverifiable promises; does the page answer the main doubts; are there repetitive blocks; is the call to action visible; does it work on phones? Table: problem, block, fix, priority.
prompts.web.content.idea: Suggest 3 structure options for a content site: [site goal]. Type: portfolio, blog or learning site. Audience: [target audience]. Materials: [content]. Task: [task]. For each: sections, how a visitor finds the right material, what's on the home page, how materials link to each other. If I gave an [example site], analyse only individual qualities (structure, mood, density, navigation) and propose an original solution rather than copying it.
prompts.web.content.spec: Draft templates for the content site “[site goal]”: a project or article page (title, summary, task, process, result, my role, captioned images, related items), a list page (filters, categories, tags, item card), an author page, a contact page without unnecessary personal data. For each template, required and optional fields. Materials: [content]. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.content.build: Build the content site templates: [content]. Technologies or platform: [technologies]. Needed: a list of items with categories and tags, an item page with previous/next navigation and related items, search by title, a contact page with a form that doesn't collect unnecessary data. Task: [task]. If the site already exists, first study the project structure, the technologies in use, any instructions in the repository and the current design. Then give a plan, change only the files that need it and list what you changed. Don't remove existing features or data without my explicit permission. Don't publish the site or change the plan, domain or access without confirmation.
prompts.web.content.review: Review the content site: [content]. Questions: is it clear on the home page whose site it is and what's here; is it easy to find material on a topic; does each project have a task, process and result; are categories and tags muddled; does navigation between items work; is there unnecessary personal data on the contact page? For each problem, a fix and a priority. Separate observations from assumptions.
prompts.web.shop.idea: Suggest 3 approaches to the catalogue for the shop “[site goal]”. Products: [content]. Audience: [target audience]. Task: [task]. For each: how categories and filters work, what's on the product card, how search and sorting work, pros and cons. Don't invent prices, stock, warranties or delivery terms.
prompts.web.shop.spec: Write out the pages of the shop “[site goal]”: catalogue (filters, sorting, no results), product card and page (fields taken from the shop's data, no invented values), comparison, empty and filled cart, step-by-step checkout with errors and confirmations, a payment and delivery FAQ based on these terms: [constraints], and a returns or question form without unnecessary personal data. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.shop.build: Build the catalogue and cart for the shop: [content]. Technologies or platform: [technologies]. Take product, price and stock data only from the project's data source; don't insert invented values. Don't connect real payment systems, change prices or send orders without my confirmation: prepare everything with test data. Task: [task]. If the site already exists, first study the project structure, the technologies in use, any instructions in the repository and the current design. Then give a plan, change only the files that need it and list what you changed. Don't remove existing features or data without my explicit permission. Don't publish the site or change the plan, domain or access without confirmation.
prompts.web.shop.review: Review the shop from this description or page links: [content]. Find: contradictions in prices, stock and timing between catalogue, product page and cart; unclear payment, delivery and returns terms; extra checkout steps; fields that collect unnecessary data; missing error messages. Check forms without submitting real data. Table: problem, page, effect on the customer, fix.
prompts.web.webapp.idea: Suggest 2 ways to organise the web app “[site goal]” for [target audience]. The user's main task: [main action]. Task: [task]. For each: a screen map, what's on the main screen after sign-in, how users add and find data, what can wait for version two.
prompts.web.webapp.spec: Specify the screens of the web app “[site goal]”: onboarding (up to 3 steps), record list (fields, filters, search, sorting, empty state), record card, add and edit (validation, saving, cancel), profile and settings, notifications. For each screen: loading, error and empty states. A separate list of actions that need confirmation (delete, send, change access) and the confirmation dialog text. Data: [content]. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.webapp.build: Build the “[page type]” screen of the web app: [content]. Technologies: [technologies]. Needed: loading, error and empty-list states, form validation with clear messages, confirmation before deleting and other irreversible actions, keyboard operation. Work with test data; don't touch real user data. Task: [task]. If the site already exists, first study the project structure, the technologies in use, any instructions in the repository and the current design. Then give a plan, change only the files that need it and list what you changed. Don't remove existing features or data without my explicit permission. Don't publish the site or change the plan, domain or access without confirmation. Task: [task].
prompts.web.webapp.review: Review the web app flows: [content]. For each flow (sign-in, add, edit, delete, search, settings), answer: is it clear what to do next; are there loading and error states; is confirmation asked before irreversible actions; can it be undone; is data lost if the network fails? Table: flow, problem, risk, fix, priority.
prompts.web.code.idea: My task: [task]. Project: [site goal], technologies: [technologies]. Suggest 2–3 ways to implement it that fit the existing stack, without switching frameworks. For each: which files and components it touches, complexity, risks, how to check the result. Pick the smallest testable first step.
prompts.web.code.spec: Turn the brief into a development plan: [content]. Stack: [technologies]. Split it into small tasks (each a few hours at most); for each: what to do, which files and components, done criteria, how to check (manually and with tests), dependencies. Mark tasks that change data, access or external services: those run only after confirmation. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.code.build: Task in the project: [task]. Technologies: [technologies]. If the site already exists, first study the project structure, the technologies in use, any instructions in the repository and the current design. Then give a plan, change only the files that need it and list what you changed. Don't remove existing features or data without my explicit permission. Don't publish the site or change the plan, domain or access without confirmation. Prefer small, testable changes over an unnecessary rewrite. Keep the current code style and design. Check the result for accessibility and responsiveness from 320 px wide. At the end, list the changed files, what was checked and the limits of the check. Extra context: [content].
prompts.web.code.review: Review the code changes: [content]. Stack: [technologies]. Checklist: does the code solve “[task]”, does it break existing features, were data or features removed without reason, semantics and accessibility (headings, labels, keyboard, focus), responsiveness (no horizontal scrolling), no secrets or passwords in the code, clear names and error handling. For each comment: file, line or fragment, fix, importance.
prompts.web.nocode.idea: Help me choose how to build the site “[site goal]” without coding. My skills: [constraints]. Features needed: [content]. Task: [task]. Suggest 3 kinds of solution (a block-based builder, AI site generation inside a builder, a design tool with publishing) and for each: what fits, what may not, which price and limit questions to check on the official site. Don't quote prices unless you're sure.
prompts.web.nocode.spec: I'm building the site “[site goal]” in a site builder: [technologies]. Make a plan: pages and blocks for each, text to fill the template based on [content], theme settings (colours [colours], fonts, spacing), a form and catalogue using the platform's features if my plan has them. Mark which features may be paid and say what to check in the platform's help. Add a pre-publication checklist. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.nocode.build: Build a draft of the site “[site goal]” in this builder from the plan: [content]. Style: [style], colours: [colours]. Use a template or page generation, then replace all text with mine and check how it looks on a phone. Task: [task]. Don't create accounts, enable a paid plan, connect a domain or payments, or publish the site without my confirmation: show me the draft first.
prompts.web.nocode.review: Make a pre-publication checklist for a site in a builder: [technologies]. Items: all text replaced, no placeholders; links and buttons work; forms send where they should (check with a test submission, no real data); phone view; page titles and descriptions for search; favicon; a privacy policy if data is collected; what stays on the free plan (e.g. a subdomain address or the platform badge — check the help pages). For each item, how to check.
prompts.web.audit.idea: Where should I start reviewing the site “[site goal]”? Audience: [target audience], main action: [main action]. Task: [task]. Suggest a review plan: which pages and flows to check first, which tools to use (browser, developer tools, contrast checker, screen reader), how much time to allow. No sign-ups to paid services.
prompts.web.audit.spec: Write an audit checklist for the existing site “[site goal]” by section: home page and first impression, main flows ([main action]), navigation on every page, links and buttons, consistency of headings, dates, prices and descriptions, responsiveness (320–1440 px), readability and contrast, keyboard accessibility, forms and error messages (tested without submitting real data), loading speed on phones. For each item, how to check and what counts as a problem. Focus: [task].
prompts.web.audit.build: Study the available code and project instructions. Review the “[page type]” page for clarity, structure, accessibility and mobile view. First list the specific problems and a fix plan and wait for my agreement. Then fix the agreed problems, keeping the current technologies ([technologies]) and features. At the end, list the changed files and the limits of the check. Don't publish the site or change paid services. Task: [task].
prompts.web.audit.review: Here are my observations about the site: [content]. Turn them into a report: a problem list sorted by impact on visitors (blocks the action, makes it harder, cosmetic). For each: where, exactly what's wrong, whether it's confirmed by observation or an assumption, a concrete fix, rough difficulty. Don't add problems I didn't mention; put questions that need checking in a separate list.

verify.web.plan: Show the plan to people from the audience or the client before starting work. The AI doesn't know your real constraints unless you wrote them down.
verify.web.structure: Test the structure with 2–3 people: ask them to find specific information and watch where they click.
verify.web.prototype: A prototype is tested with tasks, not looks: ask someone to complete the main action and note where they hesitate.
verify.web.style: Check contrast with a dedicated tool, not by eye. Before approving, look at the style with real content, not placeholders.
verify.web.ux: The AI judges from a description and general rules. The most reliable check is watching real people go through the flow.
verify.web.responsive: Check on real devices or in browser dev tools at 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 px. The AI's text is no substitute for looking.
verify.web.a11y: Go through the page with the keyboard only and turn on your phone's or computer's screen reader. Automated checks find only some problems.
verify.web.copy: Every claim about the product, price, timing or result must be true. Check the copy against the facts before publishing.
verify.web.graphics: Check the service's terms on using generated images. Don't include recognisable people, characters or logos you have no rights to.
verify.web.landing: Reviews, numbers, client logos and awards on a landing page must be real and verified. Invented data undermines trust and may break advertising law.
verify.web.content: In a portfolio, show only work you have the rights to and be honest about your role in team projects. Don't publish personal contacts unless necessary.
verify.web.shop: Take prices, stock, delivery, returns and warranty terms only from the shop's real data. Mistakes there are a direct risk for customers and for you.
verify.web.webapp: Deleting, paying, sending data to other people and changing access must require explicit confirmation. Check this in every flow.
verify.web.code: Check every change: run the site locally, open the affected pages on phone and desktop, and walk through the main flows. Keep changes on a separate branch or copy.
verify.web.nocode: Pricing, free-plan limits and publishing terms change. Check them on the builder's official pricing page before choosing and before paying.
verify.web.audit: The AI only sees what you give it: a description, screenshots or code. Re-check every “observation” it reports on the live site yourself.
